newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada hopes for Chile free trade deal very soon.
newsitem.headline: Canada hopes for Chile free trade deal very soon.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Wednesday he was very optimistic that a free trade agreement with Chile would be reached soon, possibly within days.

"It could be (this week)," Eggleton told reporters after a session of parliament. "There was lots of progress. We have definitely narrowed the issues down to a few. I'm still optimistic we'll have an agreement soon."

A Chilean negotiating team returned to Santiago on Wednesday after about 10 days of talks with Ottawa on a free trade deal between the two countries outside of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which groups Canada, the United States and Mexico.
Eggleton said a few issues remained unresolved, but declined to specify them.

Chilean officials have said one sticky issue was a rule requiring foreign investors to deposit about 30 percent of their reserves with Chile's central bank. Ottawa has been trying to get an exemption from the rule.
A planned September visit by Chilean President Eduardo Frei, which had been postponed because the free trade agreement was not reached, was rescheduled for November.
A free trade deal between Ottawa and Santiago would lay the groundwork for Chile to join NAFTA, possibly as soon as next year.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
